feed.heading: Who he was
life: Born to a noble family in Cyprus, John married and had children. When his wife and children all died at nearly the same time, he gave his life entirely to God, and in time became Archbishop of Alexandria.

He called the poor his “masters,” and had all 7,500 of the city’s needy clothed and fed each day. Owning nothing himself, he gave everything away, and died in Cyprus in 619, thanking God that nothing of those riches remained.
feed.intercession: Holy Hierarch John the Merciful, pray to God for us.
feed.caption:
Today (November 12, New Calendar) the Church remembers St John the Merciful, Patriarch of Alexandria.

He was born to a noble family in Cyprus. When his wife and children all died at nearly the same time, he took his loss as a call to forsake worldly cares and gave his life entirely to God. In time he became Archbishop of Alexandria.

On the day he became Patriarch, he had a census made of his “masters,” as he called the poor. There were 7,500 in the city, and he ordered that all of them be clothed and fed every day. When a beggar came to him four times in four disguises, he ordered him given twice as much: “Perhaps he is Jesus my Savior, who has come on purpose to put me to the test.”

He owned no property and lived in a humble cell. At his own request he returned to Cyprus, where he died in 619, giving thanks that nothing remained of the riches given him for the sake of the poor.
